title: Did your neck grow or did you just get fatter
summary: Questions the dramatic neck growth people report from neck training, noting that many document it while bulking and the neck easily stores fat. He plans to test this by growing his own neck from 16 to 18 inches at constant bodyweight during a recomp, and questions whether muscular necks really cause sleep apnea, since studies mostly involved overweight men.

claims.claim: Muscles that get almost no stimulus respond very strongly to weight training, while 'resistant' muscles are often ones used heavily in daily life that need a different stimulus.
The neck is used constantly in daily life, yet people report massive size gains once they train it with weights.
Many people who document neck training do it while bulking, and the neck readily gathers fat, making it look thicker quickly.
Many big necks have no definition or separation and look like round tubes, suggesting mostly fat rather than much muscle.
He is recomping at maintenance or a slight surplus, aiming to lose fat and gain muscle at constant bodyweight.
His neck measured 16 inches; he aims for 18 inches without gaining weight to show what two inches of pure neck muscle looks like.
He doubts that growing a muscular neck causes sleep apnea: the studies linking bigger necks to apnea mostly involved overweight men, so neck muscle may not be the cause.
